draft.title: The end of the shoguns
card: In 1853 Commodore Matthew Perry of the United States sailed warships into Edo Bay. He carried a letter asking Japan to open its ports to trade.
Japan's weapons were far weaker than the American ships' guns. The shogunate gave way and signed treaties in 1854 and later, which opened some ports to foreign trade.
Many Japanese blamed the shogun for giving in to outsiders. Support for the shogunate fell, and some samurai and nobles wanted the emperor to lead instead.
In 1868 the Meiji Restoration ended rule by shoguns. The young Emperor Meiji became the centre of government, and Japan began to modernise.
draft.remember: Foreign pressure in 1853 weakened the shogun, and in 1868 the Meiji Restoration ended shogun rule.

a.q: Why did many Japanese people lose faith in the shogunate after 1853?
opts: It had given in to foreign demands to open Japan to trade
It had started a war against the United States and lost
It had banned the emperor from holding any ceremonies
It had refused to let any samurai carry swords any longer
a.why: Perry's warships made the shogunate agree to treaties, and many Japanese saw this as weakness. The shogunate did not fight and lose a war against the United States, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about how the shogun responded to Perry's ships.

b.q: Which best describes what happened in Japan in 1868?
opts: Shogun rule ended and the emperor led the government
The shogun won back power from the emperor in a dispute
Japan shut its ports again and cancelled Perry's treaties
The United States seized Japan's government by force
b.why: The Meiji Restoration ended rule by shoguns and put the emperor at the centre of government. The treaties came earlier, in 1854 and after, and the United States did not take over Japan's government, so the other options are wrong.
b.clue: The Restoration ended one kind of ruler and put another in the centre.

a.best: It had given in to foreign demands to open Japan to trade

b.best: Shogun rule ended and the emperor led the government
